assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cavity method and message passing for random constraint-satisfaction problems turned the statistical mechanics of disordered systems into a quantitative theory of computational hardness: clustering and condensation of solutions, satisfiability thresholds, and survey propagation. It is original, conceptually clear and has lasting reach into information theory, inference and the theory of learning, which I regard as physics in the proper sense. It builds directly on replica and cavity ideas whose roots were recognised in 2021, but the specific step to algorithms and computation is distinct.
assessment.attribution: Mézard and Zecchina are the clear decisive pair for the cavity method on random constraint problems and survey propagation. Parisi, Mézard and Virasoro's earlier cavity foundations were largely recognised in 2021, and others (Monasson, Kirkpatrick, Krzakala, Zdeborova, Montanari) contributed; a two-person prize is plausible but the boundary with the 2021 citation needs care.
assessment.maturity: Mature: the thresholds have rigorous partial confirmation (Ding, Sly and Sun on k-SAT, for example), the algorithms are in use, and the framework has been stable for about two decades. Timing is good, though overlap with a recent statistical-physics prize could be read as repetition.
uncertainties: How much of the credit already falls under the 2021 recognition of disordered systems and the cavity method.
Rigorous proofs cover only parts of the predicted phase diagram; the physical picture for some regimes is not proven.
I cannot independently verify the full attribution among the many contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showing that cells organise their interior through liquid-liquid phase separation, together with a physical theory of active droplets, is a major change in cell biology and a striking use of soft-matter and non-equilibrium statistical physics. The concept is simple, original and has produced a very large literature and conceptual unification, from P granules to nucleoli.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman made the foundational P-granule observation and framed liquid-like condensates. Jülicher supplied the quantitative physical theory of active droplets. This is a natural trio, though other contributors (for example Rosen, Pappu, Weber and early colleagues of Brangwynne) complicate the attribution; credit for the theory side is also shared.
assessment.maturity: Fairly young: the paradigm is well accepted but critical discussion remains on which in vivo structures are truly phase-separated, and on functional relevance. Confirmation is wide but the interpretation is still debated, so timing is arguably slightly early.
uncertainties: Disputes about in vivo phase separation versus other assembly mechanisms.
Whether the prize would read as physics or as biology or chemistry.
Allocation between experimental discovery and theory is unsettled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theory of defect-mediated two-dimensional melting and the hexatic phase is a classic of statistical physics: a new phase with bond-orientational order and a two-step melting through unbinding of dislocations and disclinations. It is original, clear and lastingly important in condensed matter, soft matter and colloids. The topological-defect idea sits next to the 2016 recognition of Kosterlitz and Thouless.
assessment.attribution: Kosterlitz and Thouless (already awarded 2016) laid the groundwork; Halperin and Nelson, and independently Young, completed the theory of the hexatic phase and the two-stage melting. The trio is a clean and defensible configuration, with the caveat that the work is a close sequel to an already awarded discovery.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: decades of experiments on colloids, liquid crystals, and simulation confirm the hexatic phase, although the order of the melting transitions in some systems is still being debated. Recognition could be seen as long overdue and some laureates are advanced in age, which affects timeliness.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2016 prize may lessen the case.
Numerical and experimental evidence is system-dependent; the nature of melting in simple fluids was long unclear.
Age and availability of candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Inflation solves the horizon and flatness problems and, with the quantum origin of perturbations, supplies the seeds of cosmic structure through a statistical, fluctuation-based mechanism that I find compelling. It is among the most influential ideas in modern cosmology. The paradigm is very important and original.
assessment.attribution: Guth, Linde, and Mukhanov are plausible, but Starobinsky, Albrecht, Steinhardt, Sato, Chibisov and others are also decisive, and I can only choose among the credited names given. The allocation of credit is a long-standing difficulty and a major obstacle.
assessment.maturity: Predictions such as a nearly scale-invariant spectrum are consistent with CMB data, but there is no direct detection of primordial gravitational waves and alternative models remain; the specific inflationary model is unconstrained. Confirmation is indirect, so recognition may be premature.
uncertainties: No direct evidence for the inflaton or primordial tensor modes.
Credit among many originators is contested and the three-name limit is restrictive.
I am relying on my general knowledge of cosmology, not on my own expertise.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at the magic angle in twisted bilayer graphene and the discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity opened the moire materials field, a new platform for strongly correlated and topological physics. It is original, experimentally vivid and has had broad impact.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the key theoretical prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experimental discovery. This is a natural theory plus experiment pairing, although Cao and others in the experimental group and further theorists (for example Santos and Peres, Lopes dos Santos) may also be argued.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly maturing and widely reproduced, but the understanding of the superconducting mechanism is still not settled. Recognition within a few years is plausible, but the field is still developing.
uncertainties: Mechanism of superconductivity remains unresolved.
Credit among early theorists and the experimental team is contested.
Possible prematurity compared with older candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Time-reversal-invariant topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect introduced a new classification of matter based on topology and edge states, with a wide impact on condensed matter physics. It has clear originality and deep conceptual significance, and it extends the topology theme recognised in 2016.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the theoretical prediction; Molenkamp's group observed the effect in HgTe wells after the Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposal. Hasan's work on 3D topological insulators is also part of the story, but I would pick Kane, Mele and Molenkamp as a coherent core.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by many experiments (HgTe, Bi-based 3D materials), although practical consequences are less than hoped. The interpretation is stable. Timing is good.
uncertainties: Missing credit for Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Fu and Moore which is not available in this list.
Overlap with the 2016 prize on topological phases.
Relative weight of 2D versus 3D contributions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson by ATLAS and CMS completed the Standard Model and is one of the great experimental achievements; the conception and construction of the detectors was decisive. Importance is beyond doubt, though the prize for the theory was awarded in 2013.
assessment.attribution: Credit for large collaborations is inherently hard; the three named are the leaders in conceiving and building the experiments, but others (for example the spokespersons at the discovery and key accelerator people) also have claims. The statutes make this awkward.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed and mature, with timing now late. The property measurements continue. The concern is how to fairly attribute a collective discovery.
uncertainties: Collective attribution is a difficulty.
Whether the prize should reward experiment leadership rather than discovery analysis.
The credited trio may not match how others would define the key contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated matter in optical lattices (the Mott insulator transition, Fermi-Hubbard physics, single-site imaging) opened controlled experimental access to many-body models that connect to statistical physics. It is important and original, but it follows earlier recognition of cold-atom physics.
assessment.attribution: Bloch, Greiner and Esslinger carried out major experimental realisations; Zoller and Cirac made the theoretical proposals, and Jaksch is not on the list. Choosing a subset leaves out significant contributors, so allocation is unsettled.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely confirmed, with growing use as quantum simulators, but the unique science results (for example the Fermi-Hubbard phase diagram) are still being established.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier cold-atom prizes (BEC 2001, optical combs and clocks).
Theory and experimental credit allocation is unresolved.
Limit of three laureates excludes several decisive people.
